# PR #3885: Patch: holding down a card with several fusions shows a black screen

Closes #3863

Holding a fused card (a single fusion or a fusion of fusions) now opens the full-screen art drawn from the card the fusion was built on, instead of a black screen. I couldn't run a phone viewport, so this is confirmed by unit tests only.

**Cause.** A fusion id (`t-N:(a+b)`, R179) is in no catalog, so `artPlaneUri` returned `""` and every plane drew as `url("")`. The hold still opened, because a fusion takes the rarest ingredient's rarity. Desktop click-and-hold uses the same trigger, so it failed the same way. A single fusion goes through the same path, so it failed too.

**What changed** (all in `apps/web/src/cards`)
- `art/fusedArt.ts`: new `fullScreenArtId(defId, defOf)` picks the catalog card the view draws.
  - A catalog card draws as itself.
  - A fusion holding a Miner or Weapon draws its host (R3045000), through `artSubjectOf`.
  - Any other fusion draws the Dormant Starship hull if it holds one, else its last ingredient the catalog knows.
  - An id that is not a fusion is left as it is, so tokens and test ids open as before.
  - A digest id (R468) has no readable ingredients, so it returns `null`.
- `fullscreen.ts`: `useCanOpenFullScreen` also requires `fullScreenArtId` to resolve. This one gate covers the hold, the tap button, `Card`, `PoolGrid` and `OwnedCards`.
- `FullScreenArt.tsx`: the diorama and planes draw from the resolved id. If the id doesn't resolve, the view calls `onClose` from an effect and renders no planes. That covers a direct `openFullScreenArt` call that skips the gate. Intro music and the `aria-label` stay keyed to the held card's own id.

**Tests.** I added 6 unit tests in `art/fusedArt.test.tsx` and 5 in `fullscreen.test.tsx`. The hold tests render a real `Card` on a board. They cover:
- a fusion of fusions and a single fusion drawing the host's art
- release closing the view
- a digest id not opening
- `FullScreenArt` closing itself on an unresolvable id

The host in the hold tests is `core-100`, a Mythic with a diorama, so the check is that its slices draw from the host's id and none is blank. The tests cite the existing R3345000.

**Checks I ran, all green except where noted**
- `vitest` on `fusedArt.test.tsx` and `fullscreen.test.tsx`: 56 passed.
- `vitest` on `src/game/Card.test.tsx`, `src/collection`, `src/packs` and `src/cards`: 129 files, 2877 passed, 137 skipped.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`: clean once the wasm package was built.
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/cards`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok.
- I did not run the cargo checks, `patches check` or `classify`. This is a client-only change with no ruling or catalog edit.

**Decisions the plan left open**
- **Non-gear fusions** (Starship pieces and similar): they draw the Dormant Starship hull if present, else the last ingredient the catalog knows. I rejected making those cards not open, since the hull's art is correct for them.
- **Ruling:** I added none, because the fix restores what R3345000 already says.

**For the reviewer**
- `fx/takeover.ts` also calls `artPlaneBackground` with a played card's id. I left it alone, since fusions aren't played as takeovers. I haven't checked whether a fusion can reach it some other way.
- If the black screen persists on a phone after this, the next suspect is `fullscreen.css`: a plane with no background over a black backdrop.

### Its own review

Built and checked on `claude-6`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

````text
# #3863: Patch: holding down a card with several fusions shows a black screen
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## What happens

On a phone, long-pressing (holding down) a card that has several fusions on it brings up a black screen instead of the card. It was found on mobile; it is not yet known whether desktop's click-and-hold does the same.

## Expected

Holding the card opens whatever a hold normally opens for that card (the full-screen art view, R3345000, or nothing if the card can't open it) and shows the fused card correctly, never a blank or black screen. Releasing or the ✕ closes it as usual.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a phone (or a phone-sized viewport), start a game.
2. Get a card with more than one fusion on it (a fusion of fusions, e.g. several Equips or Starship fusions onto one unit).
3. Press and hold that card.
4. The screen goes black.

## Where to look (unconfirmed lead)

- The hold is `useFullScreenTrigger` in `apps/web/src/cards/fullscreen.ts`. It calls `openFullScreenArt` with the card's `defId`, and `FullScreenArtHost` / `FullScreenArt` in `apps/web/src/cards/FullScreenArt.tsx` render it as a portal over the whole page.
- A fused card's `defId` is the fusion id (`(a+b+…)`, R179, nested for a fusion of fusions). The full-screen view, `useCardLook` and `fullArtSource` may not resolve that id to art. If so, the full-screen backdrop draws with nothing on it, which would look like a black screen. Also check whether `canOpenFullScreen` should let a fusion through at all: a fusion's rarity or level may come from one ingredient. `apps/web/src/cards/fused.ts` walks a fusion to its ingredients, and `CardArt.tsx` already handles fused art (R3045000).
- Find out whether a single fusion works and only several fusions fail, and whether desktop's click-and-hold shows the same black screen.

## Done when

- Holding a card with several fusions (and a single one) never shows a black screen on a phone or on desktop: it shows the right card art or doesn't open.
- A web unit test covers the hold on a fusion of fusions, and an e2e or component check at phone width if the fix touches layout.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-6` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43443802005)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Goal.** Holding a fused card (one fusion or a fusion of fusions) opens the full-screen art view with the right picture, or doesn't open, and never shows a black screen. The cause is that `artPlaneUri` (`apps/web/src/cards/art/pictures.ts:113`) returns `""` for any id missing from the static `CATALOG`. A fusion id (`t-N:(a+b)`, R179) is never in it, so every plane becomes `url("")` and the portal draws a black screen. The hold still opens because a fusion's rarity is its rarest ingredient's (`fuse.rs` `rarest_of`), so a fusion holding a Mythic or full-art ingredient passes `canOpenFullScreen`. I did not confirm that a single fusion fails the same way, but the code path says it does. Desktop click-and-hold uses the same trigger (`game/Card.tsx` `onLongPress` → `openFullScreenArt`), so it fails the same way. The fix has two parts:
- Resolve a fusion id to the catalog card whose art it draws.
- Refuse the hold when no such card can be found.

No layout changes, so no phone-width e2e is needed. A web unit test covers the fusion of fusions.

**Files to touch**

| File | | What |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/cards/art/fusedArt.ts` | change | Add `fullScreenArtId(defId, defOf): string \| null` and the `FULL_SCREEN_ART_NONE` doc. Reuses `artSubjectOf` and `fusedParts`. |
| `apps/web/src/cards/fullscreen.ts` | change | `useCanOpenFullScreen` also requires `fullScreenArtId` to resolve, via `useDefResolver`. |
| `apps/web/src/cards/FullScreenArt.tsx` | change | `FullScreenArt` draws diorama and planes from the resolved id (and returns null if unresolvable). |
| `apps/web/src/cards/art/fusedArt.test.tsx` | change | Unit tests for `fullScreenArtId`. |
| `apps/web/src/cards/fullscreen.test.tsx` | change | Hold test on a fusion of fusions (board card), plus a digest-id test. |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, the Rust crates, `spec/` (no new ruling, see Open questions), `apps/web/src/wire/`, or `fx/takeover.ts` (a separate surface; see Risks).
Governing notes: R3345000 (full-screen view), R3350000 (diorama), R3045000 (fused art), R179 and R468 (fused ids), and CLAUDE.md rule 7. The fix is presentation only.

**Steps**

1. `apps/web/src/cards/art/fusedArt.ts`. Add imports `import { CATALOG } from "../../wire/cards.ts";` (the same module `pictures.ts:24` imports) and `import type { CardDef } from "@jackioh/shared"` if not already present. `DefOf` and `fusedParts` are already imported from `../fused.ts`. Add below `artSubjectOf`:
   ```ts
   export function fullScreenArtId(defId: string, defOf: DefOf | null): string | null
   ```
   Body, in order:
   - `if (CATALOG[defId] !== undefined) return defId;` (a catalog card draws as itself).
   - `const lookup: DefOf = (id) => defOf?.(id) ?? CATALOG[id];`
   - `const parts = fusedParts(defId, lookup);`
   - `if (parts !== null && parts.length === 1) return defId;` This is not a fusion, so leave it unchanged. Existing tests and tokens use ids outside `CATALOG`, and this keeps them opening as before.
   - If `parts === null` (a digest hides ingredients, R468), return `null`.
   - Otherwise take `const subject = artSubjectOf({ defId, name: undefined, tags: [] }, lookup);`. If `subject.defId !== defId` and `CATALOG[subject.defId] !== undefined`, return `subject.defId`. This is the host of an Equip fusion (R3045000).
   - Otherwise, for any fusion with no Miner or Weapon (for example Starship pieces), return `parts.findLast((id) => CATALOG[id] !== undefined) ?? null`, the last ingredient the catalog knows. For `[ship, piece]` that is the piece, not the hull. Pick the hull when `parts` includes `DORMANT_STARSHIP_ID` (import it from `../fused.ts`), else the last known part.
   - Pass `tags: []` because `artSubjectOf` reads only the ids and `defOf` of the parts, never the subject's own tags. Check this against the function body when you write it.
   - Add a header comment citing R3345000, R3045000 and R179, explaining why a fusion id must never reach `artPlaneUri`.

2. `apps/web/src/cards/fullscreen.ts`, `useCanOpenFullScreen`. Add `import { useDefResolver } from "./refContext.tsx";` and `import { fullScreenArtId } from "./art/fusedArt.ts";`. Call `const resolve = useDefResolver();` unconditionally at the top, before any early return. Change the final return to:
   ```ts
   return card !== null && fullScreenArtId(defId, resolve) !== null && canOpenFullScreen({ ...card, level: ... });
   ```
   This keeps the hook order fixed. It gates every caller at once: `game/Card.tsx`, `PoolGrid.tsx`, `OwnedCards.tsx`, `FullScreenButton` and `useFullScreenTrigger`. Update the docblock with one line saying a fusion no art resolves for does not open. If importing `refContext.tsx` creates a cycle, report it. `refContext.tsx` imports only `game/catalog.ts` and `glitch.ts`, so none is expected.

3. `apps/web/src/cards/FullScreenArt.tsx`, `FullScreenArt`. Add `const resolve = useDefResolver();` (import from `./refContext.tsx`) and `const artId = fullScreenArtId(defId, resolve);` at the top, after `useLocale()`. Keep every hook before any early return.
   - Replace `defId` with `artId ?? defId` in `dioramaOf(...)`, in `dioramaSliceBackground(...)` and in `artPlaneBackground(...)`. Leave `MUSIC_CARDS[defId]` and `aria-label` on `defId`/`name`. Intro music is keyed by the held card's own id, and a fusion has none.
   - Do not early-return null. Instead, when `artId === null`, call `onClose` from an effect: `useEffect(() => { if (artId === null) onClose(); }, [artId, onClose]);`. Then render nothing for the planes. This guards a view opened by a path that skipped the gate, such as a direct `openFullScreenArt` call, so a black dialog can never stay up.

4. Do not change `Card.tsx`, `PoolGrid.tsx`, `OwnedCards.tsx` or `PackOpening.tsx`. Their `defId` is passed on as-is, and the resolution lives in the view.

5. Tests (see **Tests**), then run the commands.

**Tests**

`apps/web/src/cards/art/fusedArt.test.tsx`. Add a `describe("R3345000 fullScreenArtId")` block. Reuse `fusedDef`, `defsWith`, `def()` and the constants already in the file (`BEAM_V3`, `POINTMASTER`, `MINER_V2`, `STRATOS`, `OZARK`):
- `it("R3345000 a catalog card is its own art")`: `fullScreenArtId(POINTMASTER, null)` returns `POINTMASTER`.
- `it("R3345000 a Weapon fused onto a host resolves to the host")`: `fusedDef([def(BEAM_V3), def(POINTMASTER)])` resolves to `POINTMASTER`, with `defsWith(fusion)` and with `null` (the readable id alone).
- `it("R3345000 a fusion of fusions resolves to the host")`: `inner = fusedDef([def(MINER_V2), def(POINTMASTER)], 1)` and `outer = fusedDef([def(BEAM_V3), inner], 2)` resolve to `POINTMASTER`. Use `defsWith(inner, outer)`.
- `it("R3345000 a fusion of non-gear ingredients resolves to a catalog ingredient, never to null or itself")`: use a `fusedDef([def(STRATOS), def(OZARK)])` or any two non-Weapon catalog cards, and assert the result is an id with `CATALOG[id] !== undefined`.
- `it("R3345000 a digest id hides its ingredients, so no art")`: `fullScreenArtId("t-9:#abcdef", null)` returns `null`.
- `it("R3345000 an id outside the catalog that is no fusion is left as it is")`: `fullScreenArtId("fixture-id", null)` returns `"fixture-id"`.

`apps/web/src/cards/fullscreen.test.tsx`. Add a `describe("R3345000 a fused card's full-screen hold")`. Reuse the board harness pattern at lines 529–600 (`pressAndHold`, `lift`, `WearerProvider`, `Card`, `FullScreenArtHost`). Wrap the board in `<CardDefsProvider defs={...}>` from `./refContext.tsx` with `{...CATALOG, [fusion.id]: fusion}`. Use `core-100` (a Mythic) as the host or ingredient, so the fusion's rarity is Mythic. Take `fusedDef` from `../test/fixtures.ts`. Pass the fusion def in `unitView(owner, { defId: fusion.id, … })`; check `test/fixtures.ts` `unit` for the fields that carry rarity or `def`.
- `it("R3345000 holding your own fusion of fusions opens the view drawn from its host, not a blank")`: press and hold. Assert `fullscreen-art` is present. Assert that every `.fullscreen-art-plane` has a `backgroundImage` that is not `url("")` and is not empty, and that it equals `artPlaneBackground("core-100", plane)` for that plane.
- `it("R3345000 holding a single fusion draws the host's planes")`: same with one fusion.
- `it("R3345000 releasing the held fusion closes the view")`: `lift` and assert it is gone.
- `it("R3345000 a fusion no art resolves for does not open by a hold")`: use a digest-style id (`t-9:#abc`) with rarity Mythic in the def. Assert no `fullscreen-art` appears.
- `it("R3345000 FullScreenArt over an unresolvable id closes itself")`: render `FullScreenArt` with `defId="t-9:#abc"` and `onClose` as a `vi.fn()`. Assert `onClose` was called.

These tests cite R3345000, which already exists. Add no new ruling, so `spec check` stays unchanged.

Commands, in order:
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/cards/art/fusedArt.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/cards/fullscreen.test.tsx`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/Card.test.tsx src/game/deckbuilder src/collection src/packs`. Run the suites that import `useCanOpenFullScreen`; drop any path that does not exist.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/cards`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`

**Done when**
- [ ] A hold on a fusion of fusions and on a single fusion opens a view whose planes carry the resolved host's art, never `url("")`.
- [ ] A fusion with no resolvable art does not open the view by a hold, a tap button or a direct open.
- [ ] Catalog cards, tokens and non-fusion ids outside the catalog open exactly as before, and the existing `fullscreen.test.tsx` and other suites still pass.
- [ ] The new unit tests pass; typecheck and eslint are clean.
- [ ] No `.skip`, `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore` was added, and no file outside the table was changed.
- [ ] The harness's checks (rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests) are green.
- [ ] If `cargo jackioh patches check` or `classify --claims` asks for a fragment (this is a client-only fix, so it should not), run `cargo jackioh patches "<title>"`.

**Risks**
- **Hook order.** `useDefResolver` and the new gate are called unconditionally in `useCanOpenFullScreen` and `FullScreenArt`, so no hook sits behind a condition.
- **Resolver context.** `FullScreenArtHost` renders in a portal under whatever tree mounts it. If no `CardDefsProvider` is above it, `resolve` is `null`. `fullScreenArtId` falls back to `CATALOG` and the readable id (R179), so a normal fusion still resolves. Only a digest id (R468) can fail, and it then closes rather than going black.
- **Takeover.** `fx/takeover.ts` also calls `artPlaneBackground` with a played card's defId. Fusions are not played as takeovers, so I leave it out of scope. Mention it in the report if a builder sees otherwise.
- **Hidden information (rule 7).** Resolution reads only ids the viewer already holds, from the view's definitions or `CATALOG`. It does not enforce any rule.
- **Circular import.** `fullscreen.ts` → `art/fusedArt.ts` → `art/stinkyscape.ts`. Typecheck and the vitest run will show one if it exists. If so, import `fullScreenArtId` lazily from a new `cards/fullScreenArtId.ts` instead.

**Open questions**
- Which art should a fusion of non-gear ingredients (Starship pieces) show? I chose the Dormant Starship hull if present, else the last catalog ingredient; the alternative is to not open the hold for them at all. Say so if the maintainer prefers that.
- Could the black screen on a phone also come from something other than this? I could not run a phone viewport, so I confirmed only the code path above. If the black screen persists after this fix, the next suspect is `fullscreen.css` (a plane with no background over a black backdrop).
- No new ruling is planned. The fix restores R3345000's stated behaviour, and the builder should add one only if a rules-like decision turns up.
- Difficulty: the change touches one app, with no engine, AI or migration work. It fits `difficulty:medium`.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
